properties.name: Creation of the World (Yoruba)
properties.summary: Olodumare sent Obatala to create land by pouring sand from a snail shell onto the primordial ocean. A chicken scratched the sand to spread it, forming land. Obatala shaped humans from clay but got drunk on palm wine, creating those with disabilities. Oduduwa completed the task, founding Ile-Ife, the sacred city.

properties.name: Shango — Lord of Thunder
properties.summary: Shango was a powerful king of Oyo who wielded thunder and fire. Betrayed by his subjects, he hanged himself but was deified as the orisha of thunder and justice. His three wives — Oya (wind), Oba (river), and Oshun (fertility) — became powerful orishas themselves. He is invoked for justice and strength.

properties.name: Anansi the Spider
properties.summary: Anansi the Spider wanted to own all stories. The sky god Nyame set impossible prices: capture Onini the python, Osebo the leopard, Mmoboro the hornets, and Mmoatia the invisible fairy. Through cunning rather than strength, Anansi captured them all. Nyame made all stories 'spider stories' (Anansesem).

properties.name: Ifa Divination — Orunmila's Gift
properties.summary: Orunmila, the orisha of wisdom, witnessed creation and knows the destiny of all beings. He gave humanity the Ifa divination system — 256 odu (signs) containing stories, medicines, and wisdom for every life situation. A babalawo (priest) casts palm nuts or chains to read destiny. Eshu carries messages between humans and orishas.

properties.name: Ogun Clears the Path to Earth
properties.summary: When the orishas descended from heaven to populate earth, the path was blocked by impenetrable forest. Only Ogun, god of iron, possessed the tools to cut through. He forged a machete and cleared the road. For this service, all orishas honored him. He became patron of blacksmiths, warriors, and all who use metal.
